headline: GOLD CRASHES TO $4,268 — Dollar Hits 2-Month High as October Fed Hike Odds Jump to 77%; $4,200 Support in Focus
snippet: Gold fell sharply to $4,268 per ounce on September 25 as the US dollar climbed to its highest level in two months, with CME FedWatch now placing a 77% probability on an October rate hike and 95% on December — driven by a persistent energy-shock inflation that Fed policymakers say must be confronted directly. The move puts gold 23.6% off its January 28 record of $5,589 per ounce; technically the multi-month uptrend remains intact above the $4,200 level analysts are watching, and most commentary frames the selloff as a necessary consolidation rather than a bull-market reversal.

headline: TOREX GOLD HITS 11.28 g/t AuEq OVER 31.2m IN NEW CORRIDOR — San Miguel Could Reshape Morelos Resource Inventory
snippet: Torex Gold Resources (TSX: TXG) released its Q3 2026 Morelos property update on September 24, with the new San Miguel corridor returning 11.28 g/t gold equivalent over 31.2 metres (hole MLE26-025) and 10.75 g/t AuEq over 20.2 metres (MLE26-035D). The corridor spans from Media Luna West to southeast of the operating Media Luna mine; 15,799 metres of 27,100 planned have been drilled to September 14, with all 15 rigs still active. Management says the San Miguel system is not yet fully understood and will form the centrepiece of the estimated 30,000-metre 2027 exploration budget.

headline: 49 METALS FAST-TRACKS GOLD MOUNTAIN AFTER 100% HIT RATE — 170.7m AT 0.9 g/t AU Tops Nevada Walker Lane Maiden Program
snippet: 49 Metals (ASX: 49M) announced a fast-tracked 3,500-metre follow-up RC program at its Gold Mountain project in Nevada's Walker Lane Trend, scheduled to begin October 2026, after all 22 maiden holes returned gold and/or silver mineralisation. The thickest intercept — DRC#22 at 170.7 metres of 0.9 g/t gold equivalent from 121.9 metres — is the longest continuous gold intersection recorded at the project to date and points to a large-scale epithermal system; the Walker Lane belt is one of the world's most productive gold-silver corridors and a 100% discovery hit rate in a maiden program is a notable signal for larger producers in the district.

headline: COPPER NEAR $15,070/lb COMEX — Shanghai Inventories Down 70% Since June; Physical Market Tightens as China Goes on Holiday
snippet: Comex copper held near $15,070 per pound on September 22 — within 1% of the September 9 all-time record settlement — after a sixth consecutive session of gains driven by deteriorating SHFE inventories: Shanghai cathode stocks fell to 43,900 tonnes, the lowest since 2023 and 70% below early-June levels. Chinese physical buyers stocked up ahead of the September 25–27 Golden Week closure, while LME stocks declined a further 1,625 tonnes on the same day; the compounding effect of tightening exchange inventories and the ongoing Escondida suspension in Chile leaves the copper market structurally short of metal heading into Q4.

headline: 593 g/t SILVER EQUIVALENT OVER 15m — Aya Gold & Silver Drills High-Grade Boumadine Continuity After 145,719m in 2026
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported new infill drill results from its Boumadine project in Morocco on September 22, with hole BOU-DD26-883 cutting 593 g/t silver equivalent over 15.2 metres — including 1,038 g/t AgEq over 4.2 metres — and BOU-DD26-848 returning 392 g/t AgEq over 24.3 metres. After 406 diamond drill holes totalling 145,719 metres completed in 2026, the 5.4-km Main Trend remains open in all directions; the Tizi, Imariren and 8-km Asirem trends are all scheduled for follow-up drilling later this year.

headline: 26.8% COPPER BOULDERS IN NUNAVIK — Midland + SOQUEM Open New Corridor at Nachicapau in Labrador Trough
snippet: Midland Exploration (TSXV: MD) and SOQUEM reported discovery-stage results from the Nachicapau project in the Labrador Trough, Nunavik on September 22 — including boulder grab samples grading 26.8% Cu, 0.87 g/t Au and 238 g/t Ag, and new outcrop showings at 3.03% Cu, 0.77 g/t Au and 20.0 g/t Ag in monzonite dykes. The results expand a 4-km by 1.5-km copper-gold-silver corridor established in exploration campaigns running 2022–2025 and represent the most significant surface results to date at the project.

headline: TEXAS PLANTS FIRST RARE EARTH MINING DISTRICT — Hudspeth County Leases Signal State-Level Push to Break China Supply Chain
snippet: Texas entered two new mineral leases with El Paso Minerals Corp. covering more than 1,000 acres in Hudspeth County on September 22, establishing what Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham described as the state's first dedicated rare earth mining district. The county's geology is structurally similar to rare earth districts in New Mexico and Nevada; the move is framed as part of Texas's broader push for critical mineral independence ahead of anticipated federal permitting reform, with exploration and drilling timelines still to be announced.

headline: AMERICA MINES RARE EARTHS — THE PROBLEM HAS ALWAYS BEEN WHAT COMES NEXT; China Controls Separation Choke Point Through 2028
snippet: The Washington Times argues that growing US rare earth mine output is strategically hollow as long as chemical separation and processing remain dominated by Chinese infrastructure — with combined ex-China separation capacity projected below 20% of global supply through 2028. Selling ore to Chinese processors is not supply-chain independence, the piece contends, calling for federal investment in separation and alloying capacity at the scale of the CHIPS Act; without it, new US mines will simply extend, rather than reduce, dependence on Beijing for the finished magnetic materials that go into defense hardware, EVs and wind turbines.

headline: KAZATOMPROM SLASHES 8M LB — Uranium Term Contracts Hit Record $96.50/lb; Utilities Now Financing Western Mines Directly
snippet: Kazatomprom lowered its 2026 nominal uranium output capacity by 8 million pounds to approximately 77 million pounds of U3O8 — and signalled it may exercise a further 20% downflex — pushing uranium term contract prices to a nominal all-time high of $96.50/lb, above the 2007 bull market peak, with spot at approximately $90/lb. The structural gap between what reactors require and what mines can deliver — estimated at 30–40 million pounds per year — is now forcing utilities locked out of Russian supply to provide direct project financing to junior uranium developers in Canada, Australia and the US as the only route to securing long-term fuel commitments.

headline: GOLD STRIKE WRAPS 4,014m AT FLORIN — 2.507 Moz Yukon Resource Stays OPEN; First Assay Results Expected Mid-October
snippet: Gold Strike Resources (TSXV: GSR) completed 11 diamond drill holes totalling 4,014 metres at the Florin Gold Project in Yukon's Dawson Range on September 24, with seven of those holes targeting the open south and southwest margin of the 2.507-million-ounce inferred resource. More than half the samples are already shipped to the laboratory; initial hole-by-hole assays are expected in mid-October 2026. Florin remains open in all directions and at depth — the completion announcement is a setup event for investors watching for an extension discovery in a proven, multi-million-ounce district.

headline: CHINA IMPORTED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN H1 — SWOT: Industrial Demand at Record High as Sixth Annual Deficit Deepens
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT report flags that China imported more than 790 tonnes of silver in the first half of 2026 — driven by solar panel manufacturing, EV battery packs and AI server hardware — putting global silver demand on pace for its strongest year on record, compounding the sixth consecutive structural supply deficit. Strengths include record industrial offtake and de-dollarisation buying; the identified weakness is elevated speculative positioning in gold that analysts expect to unwind before the next rally; a likely Fed pivot and ongoing clean-energy buildout are cited as the primary opportunities.

headline: AURAVELLE COMPLETES 34-HOLE NUCKULLA HILL AIRCORE — Adjacent to Barton Gold's 1.6Moz Tunkillia; RC Drilling Starts October
snippet: Auravelle Metals (ASX: AUV) completed a 3,500-metre aircore discovery program at the Nuckulla Hill Gold Project in South Australia on September 25, testing five targets in the Yarlbrinda Shear Zone adjacent to Barton Gold Holdings' (ASX: BGD) 1.6-million-ounce Tunkillia Gold Project. Early geological observations are described as encouraging; assay results are expected mid-to-late October 2026. A more capital-intensive RC drilling phase at the Sheoak, Sheoak East and Bimba targets follows, designed to test the zones most likely to host gold mineralisation at economic widths and depths.
